name: fjellrute
//: This is the workspace root. It owns three things and no application code: the Cloudflare Worker (worker/, deployed from wrangler.jsonc at this level), the verification harness (scripts/), and the toolchain that has to see the whole tree at once — eslint, tsc -b, wrangler. The browser app's own dependencies live in apps/web/package.json. The script NAMES below are load-bearing: .githooks/pre-push runs `pnpm build` and `pnpm lint` from here, so they must keep working from the root however the tree is arranged underneath.

scripts.hooks:install: git config core.hooksPath .githooks && echo 'pre-push build gate active'
scripts.dev: concurrently -n vite,worker -c cyan,yellow "pnpm -C apps/web dev" "wrangler dev"
scripts.//test:mobile: Runs immediately after test:core, because it checks the same seam from the other side: test:core proves the shared package could load on a phone, this proves the phone app only asks it for things it exports, and that the phone's scheme, host and permissions agree with the Worker's. It reads files only — no Expo, no device — so it belongs in the ordinary suite rather than behind a flag.
scripts.test:gdpr: pnpm test:deletion && pnpm test:privacy && pnpm test:policies
scripts.//test: test:core runs FIRST. Everything after it imports modules out of packages/core, so if that package has stopped being platform-free the rest of the suite is running against a package that would not load on a phone — and it would still pass, because Node has most of what a browser has. Failing early names the actual problem.
scripts.test: pnpm test:core && pnpm test:mobile && pnpm test:gdpr && pnpm test:landing && pnpm test:appbase && pnpm test:notfound && pnpm test:ratelimit && pnpm test:password && pnpm test:briefing && pnpm test:viewswitch && pnpm test:parking

//dependencies: @better-auth/expo is the SERVER half of Better Auth's Expo support, imported by worker/auth.js as `expo()`. It lives in this manifest rather than apps/mobile because the Worker is deployed from this level and is deliberately not a workspace package (see pnpm-workspace.yaml); the mobile app depends on the client half, @better-auth/expo/client, from its own manifest. It and better-auth are pinned EXACTLY, and identically, because they are one library published as two packages: they share internals and are released together, so a skew fails at runtime rather than at install. This is not hypothetical — writing both as `^1.6.23` resolved better-auth to 1.6.23 (already in the lockfile) and the plugin to 1.7.1, and pnpm reported the unmet peer rather than the mismatch. scripts/verify-mobile-app.mjs now asserts the two strings are equal, which only means something while they are exact. Raise them together. NOTE ALSO that a `//`-prefixed comment key does NOT work inside `dependencies`: pnpm treats it as a package name and tries to install it. Hence this key, at the top level.
//pnpm: Three React Native native modules, forced to the versions in expo/bundledNativeModules.json. They are peer dependencies of expo-router and @expo/ui that pnpm installs automatically, and it resolves each to the newest version satisfying the PEER's range rather than the one Expo pinned for SDK 57 — which put react-native-worklets 0.12.1 in the tree against Expo's 0.10.1 and failed the Android build in the C++ compiler, because expo-modules-core calls a WorkletRuntime::executeSync that 0.12 had removed. apps/mobile/package.json declares all three explicitly as well; this override is the other half, and it is needed because Expo's native autolinking scans the whole store, so one declared copy does not stop a second copy reaching the native build. Overriding at the root is safe because all three are React Native only — apps/web and the Worker never resolve them. react and react-dom are deliberately NOT overridden: apps/web legitimately runs a newer React than the phone, and forcing them together would break the web app in order to tidy a warning.
